summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: @servicetitan/microfront-tests@0.0.11 ships a preinstall hook (package.json scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs") that, on every `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute a 727KB bundled JavaScript file (math_init.js) at the tarball root. math_init.js is a `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle with obfuscator-style shuffled string/opcode arrays and hex-mangled identifiers; setup.mjs itself uses `_0x`-prefixed obfuscated identifiers. The filename (math_init) and the payload's purpose are unrelated to the package's advertised functionality: the dist/ entry point is a small test helper that only re-exports ts-mockito and a couple of container/utils modules. The advertised @servicetitan scope is a well-known enterprise publisher, but the shipped payload is decoupled from the advertised public surface — consistent with a compromised or malicious publish smuggling a dropper into a test-helper package. Invocation via a freshly downloaded alternate runtime evades Node-oriented scanners and hands arbitrary code execution to whatever math_init.js contains, on any host that runs `npm install` on this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
